notes: EBIT is modeled as GAAP “Operating earnings” from Cardinal Health’s consolidated statements of earnings. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/721371/000072137125000079/cah-20250630.htm))

D&A is modeled from cash flow “Depreciation and amortization,” and capex from cash flow “Additions to property and equipment.” ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/721371/000072137125000079/cah-20250630.htm))

NWC is computed as: (Current assets − Cash and equivalents) − (Total current liabilities − Current portion of long-term obligations and other short-term borrowings). This is a modeling approximation of operating working capital and may differ from any company-defined NWC metric. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/721371/000072137125000079/cah-20250630.htm))

Tax rate (0.21) is a normalized modeling assumption because GAAP effective tax rates are volatile year to year due to discrete items; GAAP tax expense and EBT are available in filings. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/721371/000072137125000079/cah-20250630.htm))

NOL balance uses the sum of gross loss and credit carryforwards disclosed (federal/state/international) because the filing provides gross carryforwards rather than a single consolidated “NOL” figure; credits are included in the carryforward totals, and utilization percent is assumed at 0.80 for the DCF schedule. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/721371/000072137125000079/cah-20250630.htm))
Peer comps multiples are left null because consistent EV/NTM Revenue and EV/NTM EBITDA inputs were not accessible in a non-paywalled way during this run.

catalysts: Sustained execution against multi-year improvement initiatives (profit/cash flow generation) translating into higher-than-modeled earnings durability. ([s201.q4cdn.com](https://s201.q4cdn.com/566741227/files/doc_events/2025/Jun/2025-Investor-Day-Press-Release.pdf))

Further guidance raises and/or operating outperformance (volume mix, cost optimization), particularly in Pharma and the “Other” growth areas. ([newsroom.cardinalhealth.com](https://newsroom.cardinalhealth.com/2026-02-05-Cardinal-Health-Reports-Second-Quarter-Fiscal-Year-2026-Results-and-Raises-Outlook))

Ongoing shareholder returns (repurchases) supported by disciplined leverage and free cash flow. ([newsroom.cardinalhealth.com](https://newsroom.cardinalhealth.com/2026-02-05-Cardinal-Health-Reports-Second-Quarter-Fiscal-Year-2026-Results-and-Raises-Outlook))
company_overview: Cardinal Health is a global healthcare services and products company with segments spanning pharmaceutical distribution/specialty services and medical products distribution/manufacturing, plus Other businesses. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/721371/000072137125000079/cah-20250630.htm))

The model uses GAAP operating earnings as EBIT and reflects the company’s historically low (but improving) operating margin profile driven by distribution/supply chain economics. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/721371/000072137125000079/cah-20250630.htm))

Working-capital structure is modeled with negative net working capital (distributor-like), which typically supports cash conversion despite modest EBIT margins. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/721371/000072137125000079/cah-20250630.htm))
current_context: Q2 FY26: revenue of $65.6 billion (+19% YoY) and GAAP operating earnings of $707 million (+29% YoY). ([newsroom.cardinalhealth.com](https://newsroom.cardinalhealth.com/2026-02-05-Cardinal-Health-Reports-Second-Quarter-Fiscal-Year-2026-Results-and-Raises-Outlook))

Q2 FY26: Cardinal raised FY26 non-GAAP diluted EPS guidance to $10.15-$10.35 (+23%-26%). ([newsroom.cardinalhealth.com](https://newsroom.cardinalhealth.com/2026-02-05-Cardinal-Health-Reports-Second-Quarter-Fiscal-Year-2026-Results-and-Raises-Outlook))

Cardinal completed an annual baseline share repurchase of $750 million during the quarter/year-to-date context. ([newsroom.cardinalhealth.com](https://newsroom.cardinalhealth.com/2026-02-05-Cardinal-Health-Reports-Second-Quarter-Fiscal-Year-2026-Results-and-Raises-Outlook))
investment_highlights: Base case ties forecast revenue growth to a normalization from the FY2024 OptumRx expiration impact and continued scaling in higher-growth parts of the portfolio, with growth tapering toward mature rates. ([newsroom.cardinalhealth.com](https://newsroom.cardinalhealth.com/2026-02-05-Cardinal-Health-Reports-Second-Quarter-Fiscal-Year-2026-Results-and-Raises-Outlook))

EBIT margin assumptions move modestly toward ~1.0% as cost optimization and mix stabilization offset the inherently low-margin distribution base. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/721371/000072137125000079/cah-20250630.htm))

Capex is held at a stable sales ratio consistent with management’s FY26 capex ~$600 million communicated in investor materials. ([s201.q4cdn.com](https://s201.q4cdn.com/566741227/files/doc_events/2025/Jun/2025-Investor-Day-Press-Release.pdf))

Negative modeled NWC (accounts payable/receivables dynamics) is maintained through the forecast to avoid overstating free-cash conversion. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/721371/000072137125000079/cah-20250630.htm))
key_risks: Customer contract or payer mix changes (and related working capital swings) that pressure revenue and cash generation versus the base case. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/721371/000072137125000079/cah-20250630.htm))

Margin compression from pricing pressure, tariffs/cost inflation, and unfavorable operating leverage. ([newsroom.cardinalhealth.com](https://newsroom.cardinalhealth.com/2026-02-05-Cardinal-Health-Reports-Second-Quarter-Fiscal-Year-2026-Results-and-Raises-Outlook))

Tax and legal/regulatory risks, including utilization and timing uncertainty of loss/credit carryforwards. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/721371/000072137125000079/cah-20250630.htm))

Terminal value uses an EBITDA exit-multiple framework (exit_multiple) with a moderate terminal multiple assumption to reflect durable but competitive healthcare distribution cash flows.
